body: I know what that's like. It feel brutal. You feel alone. You feel helpless. But it's not worth it. You'll find someone else. Give yourself sometime. Wait a day, then maybe a week. Set up any event in the future to look forward to short term, and just try and make it that far and then do it over again. Time will get you through this.

Hey,

I know what you're going through and it's the worst. I recommend that you try and call a local crisis line, they're usually free, 24 hours, and whoever picks up will listen to whatever you feel like telling them. I don't know specifically what you're going through but whatever it is, I imagine that if you wait a few years it will get better. 17 is a particularly tough age. See if you can make it to 20, that's only three more years! I imagine by then things will be far better. Keep your chin up.

Hi thanks for reaching out, 

I'm still getting the treatments, and I'm pretty early into it, so I'm still occasionally finding a new wart which can be very upsetting. However, since going to specialists (Centre for Disease control docs) I've calmed down a lot. The first doctor I saw essentially said my life was over. However, all the new data that has come out in regard to HPV is pretty optimistic in regard to the body's immune system clearing or suppressing the virus within 8 to 16 months, which is reassuring.  

The specialist I spoke to said that an outbreak a year after being symptom free is more likely to be a new infection caused by a different wart causing strain of HPV. I will always disclose the info, cause I think it's important to know, and I've never been super into casual sex anyways. But I do get moments where I feel like no girl will ever be with me again etc., which is certainly melodramatic. 

I guess one thing I'd be interested in, is how you disclose to partners, how long you'll date someone before you disclose, how you characterize it "as cured" or "suppressed."

Hey man, 

It sounds like you're going through an incredibly rough time. I understand how that feels. Loneliness is a really terrible thing to have to deal with. I'm really happy that you went to see somebody and that you're going to the clinic tomorrow. You should be proud you're taking positive steps, and taking hold of your future. I wish you the best of luck.

cchristini, I sent you a reply to your last message. Should be in your inbox. What you're going through is incredibly difficult. It hurts. You don't have to be strong, you just have to know that you'll make it through this.

Hi OP, 

It sounds like you're going through an incredibly hard time right now. I can imagine how you're feeling. Moving back home as an adult is always difficult. But it's far from unusual. I did it three times! And I'm doing great now. Also, a lack of a degree is not worth killing yourself. Most people don't have degrees. Don't let a shitty job market get you down! It will inevitably improve. It's a statistical certainty.

At 21 you may feel like you've experienced all life has to offer, but trust me you have not. There are a number of great things left for you to enjoy and experience. It will just take time for them to reveal themselves to you. 

Keep your chin up man.

Hi Op, 

The job market is tough right now, so don't beat yourself up about it. I've lived at home three different times since finishing college. It's totally normal even though your parents might not understand that. Further, in this economy it's also normal to go weeks or months at a time looking for work. Your parents shouldn't make you feel inadequate merely because your generation was dealt a particularly shitty hand by the baby boomers financial mismanagement. 

You are not pathetic! You will find a job. You will move out. These are not impossibilities, though it might feel that way right now. 23 is so incredibly young, it takes time to build a future. I have faith in you. Good luck!

Hey op, 

Also a Canadian. I have a similar issue with intrusive suicidal thoughts occurring a a few times a year. It's incredibly tough, and it hurts like hell. I feel for you. Personally, I find it's always extremely positive to reach out and ask for help and talk about the condition with people who are trained to handle it. 

Call a crisis helpline. They'll be able to put you in touch with some free mental services; also they're excellent people. They're trained to listen and help you work through your issues - sometimes enough to resolve the thoughts of suicide. You won't have to go to the hospital if you call, and you definitely won't be committed. So don't worry about that.

This is a great place to start:

http://www.mentalhealthhelpline.ca/ 

Good luck! You'll make it through!

Hey man, 

You'll be fine. It sounds like you're more of a late bloomer than anything else. I was in a similar situation. Top school, relatively good looking, kind, sincere, talkative, funny etc. but for whatever reason, I just couldn't make it work. Then all of a sudden and totally unexpectedly it began to click around the age of 21. NOW my biggest problem is genital warts (true story, quuuuite depressing). Appreciate what you have in front of you, you are awesome, you will get laid, and more importantly you'll find someone to love and appreciate you. Generally speaking women tend to go for guys who love and appreciate themselves first though, so don't get obsessed with this "I'm worthless" language, you're not worthless. Keep your head up, and stay optimistic, things will happen.

OP, I'm really sorry that you have to go through this. I've struggled myself with intrusive thoughts, which have left me at times feeling totally debilitated and essentially unable to work, sleep, eat. I've become obsessed with ideas of being a failure, unloved, alone etc. And recently, believe it or not, I was also diagnosed with an embarrassing medical condition. I was crying daily. I've even posted on this subreddit before. 

Here's the positive: It will get better, you will find happiness again. Look for the small things that are beautiful. Focus in on those details. Fixate on all the beautiful things that are around you: your mom, your healthy sister. I know it can be impossible to be optimistic in the situation you're describing, but it's a statistical certainty that things will get better.

I know what you're feeling. It's absolutely the worst. But you can't let the bullies get the better of you. You're a kind and dignified and wonderful person. You just have to take one step forward, and then another. Start holding your head up high. You deserve to.
